title: [Parser] Ambiguous ampersand is incorrectly handled in tokenizer
body:
This is how [ambiguous ampersand](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/syntax.html#syntax-ambiguous-ampersand) is handled in the spec currently:
> If the temporary buffer consists of a U+0026 AMPERSAND character (&) followed by a sequence of one or more ASCII alphanumerics and a U+003B SEMICOLON character (;), then this is a parse error.

(see https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/syntax.html#named-character-reference-state).

The issue is that `temporary buffer` should contain only characters that match one of the character references:

> Consume the maximum number of characters possible, with the consumed characters matching one of the identifiers in the first column of the named character references table (in a case-sensitive manner). Append each character to the temporary buffer when it's consumed.

Therefore, condition for the ambiguous ampersand will never be met: if `temporary buffer` contains characters and a semicolon then there was a match for a character reference, since there are no character references with a semicolon in the middle. Moreover, even if we'll solve issue with a trailing semicolon in the `temporary buffer` it will be insufficient to correctly report error for the ambiguous ampersand: we will only report errors for incomplete well-known character references. 

The correct way to handle this will be introduction of the additional ambiguous ampersand state, to which we'll switch if no match was made. And in this state:
- on ASCII alphanumeric: append character to the `temporary buffer`
- on SEMICOLON: If the `temporary buffer` contains more than one character (i.e. at least one ASCII alphanumeric, first one is always AMPERSAND as per https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/syntax.html#character-reference-state) then report a parse error. Reconsume in the character reference end state.
- on anything else: reconsume in the character reference end state.
